observation.visible_scene: A wide seascape at sunset/sunrise: a bright round sun sits just above a flat, calm horizon under a gradient orange-gold sky with a few thin clouds. A small dark island/rocky landmass silhouettes on the right horizon, with a fainter low landmass on the far left. A vertical column of shimmering golden reflection stretches down the water from the sun toward the foreground, which shows gentle ripples. The overall framing (horizon line, sun, island, clouds) stays fixed across the clip.
visible_changes: The sea surface ripples continuously: wave crests and troughs in the foreground shift and reform from frame to frame.
The sun's glittering reflection column fluctuates in brightness and pattern; individual bright specular glints appear, move, and fade along the vertical path below the sun.
The sun's position relative to the horizon, the right-hand island, the left landmass, and the clouds remain essentially unchanged throughout the excerpt (no perceptible descent or shift).
outside_clip_unknowns: The actual lowering of the sun below the horizon is not visible within this short segment, so the rate/progress of the sunset is unknown.
Whether the camera later pans, zooms, or tilts, or whether the clip's true start/end contain other motion, is unknown.
Any wind, current, or other cause of the water motion is not shown.
uncertain_details: No camera motion is detectable; the horizon and fixed landmarks hold constant pixel positions, but extremely slow drift cannot be fully ruled out.
The sun does not visibly set during these ~2.67 s, so the clip captures an ongoing sunset only via its static lighting, not via measurable sun movement.
